subject: Energy
title: Flow Batteries
description: A fast breakdown of Flow Batteries for builders.

hook.text: Flow batteries store energy in liquid electrolytes held in external tanks—the bigger the tanks, the more energy stored.

buildup.text: Two liquids flow through a cell stack, exchanging ions across a membrane—reversing the flow recharges the battery.

discovery.text: Vanadium redox flow batteries are the most mature—they last 20+ years with virtually no capacity degradation.

twist.text: Power is set by the cell stack size; energy is set by the tank volume—they scale independently, unlike lithium-ion.

climax.text: Flow batteries excel at 4–12 hour durations—filling the gap between lithium-ion (short) and hydrogen (seasonal).

punchline.text: Bigger tanks, more hours—flow batteries scale with simple plumbing.

quiz.question: How do flow batteries increase storage duration?
